newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June S&P 500s end higher ahead of labor data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June S&P 500s end higher ahead of labor data.

text.p: U.S. June Standard & Poor's 500 futures contracts closed slightly higher, supported by gains in the Nasdaq composite ahead of U.S. March labor reports on Friday, traders said.
"The Nasdaq helped keep S&Ps afloat," one market source said.
Cash and futures S&Ps diverged from the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which fell more than 80 points in the afternoon.
"You had select stocks like IBM dragging the Dow Industrials lower," he said.
Other sources said the Dow Industrials were finally catching up with losses in S&Ps, and that both indices were now poised to test the key 10-percent correction levels.

The June S&P contract needs to fall about nine points to hit 745.00, a 10-percent correction from its all-time high of 827.80. A drop of about 77 points to 6,400 would represent a 10 percent correction in the Dow, several traders said.
Every S&P point equals about 8.50 Dow points.
"There is a lot of nervousness about earnings and about the Fed raising rates," one S&P futures floor trader said. "S&Ps still look queasy even though we are higher."
He noted that June S&Ps will be unchanged for the year when the contract tests 740.00, the January 2 low.
Several traders noted that one major U.S. dealer was selling stocks and buying bonds in an asset allocation after the 30-year long bond closed with a yield above seven percent.
"It's been a long time since the 30-year bond closed with a yield richer than seven percent on a monthly basis," he said. "And you are seeing a lot of model-driven asset allocators dropping stocks."
A large arbitrage buy program finally materialized after much pit talk once U.S. bond futures closed.
Arbitrage buy programs were seen at 6.83 points to cash, but June S&Ps' premium by the close had narrowed well below fair value at 6.00 points.
In addition, the contract's moderately higher close belied the massive, sudden price swings. Twice in the session June S&Ps swung more than seven points within 30 minutes.

Traders attributed the volatile trade to nervousness ahead of Friday's U.S. nonfarm payrolls report. Payrolls are expected to rise an average of 196,000, up from Reuters previous average estimate of 182,000 and against February's increase of 339,000.
The unemployment rate for March is forecast to fall to 5.2 percent from 5.3 percent in February.

At the end of pit trade, June S&P 500s were up 2.55 points at 753.85, NYSE Composites were up 0.35 at 396.75, KCBT Value Lines were off 0.05 at 679.45, Nikkei 225s were 35 higher at 18,115, Midcap 400s were up 0.45 at 250.95 and Nasdaq 100s were 27.25 higher at 814.50.
